title.de: Das Passiv: is baked, was built
title.it: Il passivo: is baked, was built
title.en: The passive: is baked, was built

rule.sl:
**Trpnik** rabiš, ko je pomembno, kaj se zgodi, ne kdo to naredi: **be** + deležnik. Slovenščina tu pogosto reče *pečejo* ali *se peče*.

Sedanjik: **is, are**: **The bread is baked here.** (Kruh pečejo tukaj.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** Preteklik: **was, were**: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Most so zgradili leta 1720.) **The letters were sent yesterday.**

Deležnik je pri pravilnih glagolih **-ed** (baked, mended), pri drugih svoj: **built, made, sold, written, taken, stolen, broken**. Ljudje rečejo tudi *It was broke*, *It was took*; pisava hoče **broken**, **taken**. V govoru je pravilno tudi **got**: **My van got stolen.**

Kdo je to naredil, pove **by**: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Vrata je popravil gospod Dixon.) Če ni pomembno, ga izpustiš.

Vprašanje in zanikanje naredi be, brez do in did: **Was the letter sent?** **The gate wasn't closed.** **When was the bridge built?**

Po **can** in **must**: **be** + deležnik: **The gate can be opened from inside.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.**
rule.de:
**Das Passiv** nimmst du, wenn wichtig ist, was geschieht, nicht wer es tut: **be** + Partizip. Vorsicht: *wird gebacken* heißt **is baked**, nicht *will*.

Gegenwart: **is, are**: **The bread is baked here.** (Das Brot wird hier gebacken.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** Vergangenheit: **was, were**: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Die Brücke wurde 1720 gebaut.) **The letters were sent yesterday.**

Das Partizip ist bei regelmäßigen Verben **-ed** (baked, mended), bei den anderen ein eigenes: **built, made, sold, written, taken, stolen, broken**. Man sagt auch *It was broke*, *It was took*; geschrieben steht **broken**, **taken**. Gesprochen ist auch **got** richtig: **My van got stolen.**

Wer es getan hat, sagt **by**, nicht *from*: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Das Tor wurde von Mr Dixon repariert.) Ist es nicht wichtig, fällt es weg.

Frage und Verneinung macht be, ohne do und did: **Was the letter sent?** **The gate wasn't closed.** **When was the bridge built?**

Nach **can** und **must**: **be** + Partizip: **The gate can be opened from inside.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.**
rule.it:
**Il passivo** si usa quando conta che cosa succede, non chi lo fa: **be** + participio. L'italiano dice spesso *si fa* o *viene fatto*.

Presente: **is, are**: **The bread is baked here.** (Qui si fa il pane.) **Eggs are sold at the farm.** Passato: **was, were**: **The bridge was built in 1720.** (Il ponte fu costruito nel 1720.) **The letters were sent yesterday.**

Il participio è **-ed** per i verbi regolari (baked, mended), gli altri ne hanno uno loro: **built, made, sold, written, taken, stolen, broken**. Si dice anche *It was broke*, *It was took*; per iscritto si usa **broken**, **taken**. A voce va bene anche **got**: **My van got stolen.**

Chi l'ha fatto lo dice **by**, cioè *da*: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** (Il cancello è stato riparato da Mr Dixon.) Se non conta, si lascia fuori.

Domanda e negazione le fa be, senza do e did: **Was the letter sent?** **The gate wasn't closed.** **When was the bridge built?**

Dopo **can** e **must**: **be** + participio: **The gate can be opened from inside.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.**
rule.en:
Use **the passive** when what happens matters more than who does it: **be** + the participle.

Present: **is, are**: **The bread is baked here.** **Eggs are sold at the farm.** Past: **was, were**: **The bridge was built in 1720.** **The letters were sent yesterday.**

The participle is **-ed** for regular verbs (baked, mended); the others have their own: **built, made, sold, written, taken, stolen, broken**. People also say *It was broke*, *It was took*; writing wants **broken**, **taken**. In talk **got** is right too: **My van got stolen.**

**by** says who did it: **The gate was mended by Mr Dixon.** If that doesn't matter, leave it out.

be asks and says no, with no do or did: **Was the letter sent?** **The gate wasn't closed.** **When was the bridge built?**

After **can** and **must**: **be** + the participle: **The gate can be opened from inside.** **Dogs must be kept on a lead.**
